- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in subsequent periods.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by overcorrection, cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.3) and price is trending down, model often underestimates drop; add 2–5% downward bias to forecast if recent sentiment is bearish.
- If model forecast is > 10% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion correction: subtract 1–3% per day until convergence to recent 14-day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment swing midpoint (e.g., if sentiment shifts from +1 to -1, forecast should reflect 1–2 day lag in price reversal).
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after model peak, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days to account for sentiment-driven volatility.
